newsitem.title: SPAIN: Irish and Spanish films tie at San Sebastian.
newsitem.headline: Irish and Spanish films tie at San Sebastian.

text.p: An Irish romp about travelling salesmen and a Spanish exploration of xenophobia tied for the "Golden Shell" award for best film at Europe's oldest film festival on Saturday.
"Trojan Eddie", directed by Gillies Mackinnon, and "Bwana", directed by Imanol Uribe, were selected from 18 entries to the 44th San Sebastian film festival in northern Spain.
The "Silver Shell" for best director went to Peruvian director Francisco Lombardi for his thriller "Bajo la Piel" (Under the Skin), a co-production by Spain, Peru and Germany.
The jury's special prize went to German entry "Engelchen" (Little Angel), directed by Helke Misselwitz.
British actor Michael Caine won the best actor award for his role as a professional safe-blower in "Blood and Wine".
The U.S. thriller, directed by Bob Rafelson and co-starring Jack Nicholson, explores a family's dark side and has been described by critics as sordid and sadistic.
Argentinian actress Norma Aleandro won the prize for best actress for her role in "Sol de Otono" (Autumn sun), a story of love between older people.
